headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: Cursor can ingest shared workspace/clipboard content while social-auto-upload can act on unverified outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and uses MCP; social-auto-upload handles files and account workflows. A shared local filesystem or copied content can carry attacker-controlled instructions into Cursor, which may then influence automation. The pair lacks provenance tracking, so interaction is unsafe by default.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or copied content during one task
IF social-auto-upload content is pasted into Cursor without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Use separate workspaces or directories for each agent
Require manual review of any text copied from social-auto-upload before Cursor reads it
Turn off MCP for tasks that ingest untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared files and messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers; social-auto-upload touches account data and media files. If they share a workspace or clipboard, sensitive code or account artifacts can flow from one agent into the other and then out via Cursor's backend calls.
conditions: IF account data or media files are placed in the same local workspace as source code
IF clipboard contents from one agent are reused by the other
mitigations: Keep account files and code in separate directories
Avoid copying secrets or account data through the clipboard
Restrict Cursor to non-sensitive projects when social-auto-upload is active
Review outbound prompts before Cursor sends them to model providers
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data separation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; social-auto-upload is file-oriented and networked but does not write files. The main conflict is shared mutable workspace state: Cursor can change files that social-auto-upload later consumes, causing racey or inconsistent uploads. Uncertainty is limited, but the shared filesystem path makes conflict plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or account file
IF Cursor edits files while social-auto-upload is reading them
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Serialize edits and uploads so only one agent touches a file at a time
Avoid running Cursor in Yolo mode on shared repos
Check in or snapshot files before handing them to social-auto-upload
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate or edit content that social-auto-upload may then upload or publish, and social-auto-upload has network egress to external platforms. If B treats A's output as authoritative, a mistaken caption, filename, or metadata change can cascade into public posting or account actions. The pair therefore has a dangerous default handoff path.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes files or metadata produced by Cursor without a verification step
IF Cursor edits upload payloads that are later published by social-auto-upload
mitigations: Require human review before upload
Compare generated metadata against source files before publishing
Use a staging account for test uploads
Log and diff Cursor edits before social-auto-upload runs
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, clipboard contents, and broad model-provider egress, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media. If account data or regulated content is placed into Cursor's broader third-party inference path, retention and residency obligations can diverge from the uploader's local workflow. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated account data or personal media is opened in Cursor
IF the same data is then processed by social-auto-upload under different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor projects
Use non-sensitive test accounts for uploads
Review vendor privacy terms before sharing account data
Minimize clipboard use for personal data
requires-engineering: document retention and residency boundaries
